description_full: Ero Copper Corp. engages in the exploration, development, and production of mining projects in Brazil. Its flagship asset includes Caraíba operations that comprise the production and sale of copper concentrates located in Bahia State, Brazil, as well as gold and silver produced and sold as by-products. The company was incorporated in 2016 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.
ceo_bio: Mr. Makko  DeFilippo | President, CEO & Director | Age 38 | Compensation: $1.1M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: Ero Copper Corp. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $3.0B market cap on $786M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -5.3pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 10% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 44%.

The business throws off $132M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.48× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.1×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.3% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
